summary: Examples of lineinfile: setting SELinux mode, removing sudoers lines, replacing hosts entries with regex or literal strings, changing Apache's Listen port, inserting comments, creating files, using backrefs, and validating sudoers with visudo.
questions: How do I set SELINUX=enforcing with Ansible?
How do I change Apache's listen port with lineinfile?
How do I add a sudoers line safely with validation?
How do I keep part of a line and change a value with backrefs?
How do I avoid backref conflicts with variables in the line?

answer_card.title: lineinfile examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/selinux/config
    regexp: '^SELINUX='
    line: SELINUX=enforcing
- ansible.builtin.lineinfile: {path: /etc/sudoers, state: absent, regexp: '^%wheel'}
- ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf
    regexp: '^Listen '
    insertafter: '^#Listen '
    line: Listen 8080
- ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/sudoers
    regexp: '^%ADMIN ALL='
    line: '%ADMIN ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL'
    validate: /usr/sbin/visudo -cf %s
- ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /tmp/config
    regexp: ^(host=).*
    line: \g<1>{{ hostname }}
    backrefs: yes
```
Use `\g<1>` instead of `\1` when the following text could be a digit.
